design.principle: The server computes the predicate. The BFF consumes the answer. No fourth copy of subscriptionTierGrantsStudio.

changes.change: peEntitlementBaseBody gains a computed studioGranted: subscriptionTierGrantsStudio(snap.subscriptionTier), APPENDED LAST so the pinned R1 field order ahead of it is byte-identical. Dev role needs no special case: resolvePeEntitlement already maps devRole to subscriptionTier team (lines 120-124), so the one predicate covers it.
PeEntitlementResult ok-branch and PeEntitlementDetail carry studioGranted: boolean | null, parsed from the server body. REQUIRED field, not optional, so tsc forces every call site to supply it.
Both resolvers require studioGranted === true. Three-state, never two.

SITEPLAN, SPPDF, SPDXF, SPIFC gain studioGated: true. catalogStatus is deliberately LEFT as ready: REC already ships studioGated true with catalogStatus ready, so the two fields are not coupled, and flipping catalogStatus would churn the group snapshot in reports-catalog.test.ts:26 for no behavioural gain.

design.threeStateRationale: studioGranted absent from the server response is UNMEASURED, not false. Absent, zero and unmeasured are three different states. true gives serve; false gives 402 studio_required naming Studio, distinguishable from the free-tier 402 payment_required; null gives 503 entitlement_contract_incomplete, which names the real cause (this BFF is talking to a cortex-api that predates the field) instead of showing a paying customer a paywall for a deploy-order problem. Fail closed in all three, honest in all three.

predicateDefinitionCount.countingRule: occurrences of the string 'function subscriptionTierGrantsStudio' across both repos, excluding node_modules

adversarialReview.risk: DEPLOY ORDER. If the PE BFF ships to Vercel before cortex-api ships the studioGranted field, every Studio and Team customer hits the null branch and gets a 503 on CAD and terrain.
adversarialReview.disposition: ACCEPTED AND DECLARED, not mitigated by fail-open. Required order is stated as a blocking condition in the close: cortex-api (LDT) first, verified on the live /entitlement body, THEN the Vercel BFF deploy. The alternative, treating absent as granted, preserves the exact leak this card exists to close; treating absent as false would tell a paying Studio customer they need to pay, which is a false statement about their account.

adversarialReview.risk: The dev bypass short-circuits ahead of the Studio check in both resolvers, so an armed bypass still serves CAD to a free session.
adversarialReview.disposition: UNCHANGED BY DESIGN. That is the existing operator QA path and it is env/secret-armed server-side (pe-export-dev-bypass.ts: PE_EXPORT_DEV_BYPASS=1 or a header matching PE_EXPORT_DEV_BYPASS_SECRET), never client-reachable. Widening this card to the bypass would be scope creep. Recorded so the exclusion is deliberate rather than unnoticed.

adversarialReview.risk: Acceptance item 6 gates SPPDF (the site-plan PDF) to Studio, but the pricing matrix row is 'Site plan CAD, DXF, IFC' (pricing.ts:167) and Studio's sold feature string is 'site-plan CAD (DXF, IFC)' (pricing.ts:108). Neither names PDF.
adversarialReview.disposition: FOLLOW THE CARD, REPORT THE SEAM. The card names SPPDF explicitly, and SITEPLAN is ONE catalog row with formatLabel 'PDF, DXF, IFC'; a per-format split would require splitting the row, which is a bigger design change than this card scopes, and any pricing change is listed as explicitly not this card. Note that Solo does NOT lose the site-plan drawing: the X-ray PDF a Solo subscriber can still export appends the site-plan sheets (reports-catalog.ts:88-89). What Studio sells is the openable file. The planner is asked to rule on whether the standalone site-plan PDF stays Studio or drops to Solo.
